resources.string: Every button opens the playground with that item switched on. Change anything there, then show the result.
Snap to position after a scroll or fling
Select the cell a snap lands on
ListView lays one view per cell. GridView packs a fixed number of views into every row or column. GridPatternView sizes each view from a repeating pattern of shapes.
The axis the content scrolls along. A vertical GridView fills rows; a horizontal one fills columns.
The gap between neighbouring cells. Space at the outer edges comes from the view\'s own padding.
Paints a line on every edge two cells share, centred in the cell spacing, and none at the outer boundary of the content.

After a drag or fling, settles the nearest cell on the snap position; a tapped cell snaps there too, and setSelection jumps. With onScreen nothing settles, but a tap still brings its cell fully on screen and setSelection still jumps.
Where a cell settles, a page lands and setSelection jumps to, and how far the first and last cells can be pulled in from the edges.
Circular scroll forces onScreen, so center, start and end no longer differ: all three still settle the nearest cell on an edge, and onScreen alone turns that settle off.

Keeps the content inside the view: the first cell stops at the start edge and the last cell at the end edge, and content that fits the view sits at the snap position instead of scrolling. Needs a snap position other than onScreen, which already keeps the content inside, and no circular scroll, which has no ends.
After the last cell comes the first again, so the content has no ends to pull against.
Only a fling turns a page. Snapping to a position other than onScreen is on, so a drag released slowly settles on a cell too.
Only a fling turns a page; a drag released slowly stops where it is. To always rest on a page, also snap to a position other than onScreen.
How far one fling pages: every cell that fits the viewport whole, or a fixed number of cells. Needs ViewPager.
Selects the cell a snap lands on. Needs snapping; with onScreen a snap only lands when the content is pushed against an end, which circular scroll has none of.
Moves the selection to the cell nearest the snap position while the content is still moving. Needs a snap position other than onScreen; snapping itself is not needed.
How many views share a row (vertical) or a column (horizontal).
top and bottom place a view shorter than its row, such as one whose caption wraps. left and right place a row narrower than the width: the short last row.

top and bottom place a view shorter than its row, such as one whose caption wraps. left and right would place a row narrower than the width, but the photos fill every row: %1$d of them, %2$d to a row.
top and bottom place a column shorter than the height: the short last column. left and right would place a view narrower than its column, and these fixed-width cells never are.

top and bottom would place a column shorter than the height, but the photos fill every column: %1$d of them, %2$d to a column. left and right would place a view narrower than its column, and these fixed-width cells never are.
The length of one pattern unit along the scroll axis over its breadth across it; 1.0 makes square units. Every shape in the pattern spans whole units.
The repeating groups of shapes the views fill, in adapter order. Defined in code; see PatternOption.
